speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; to determine the cause, have these symptoms been present for a few days or several weeks?

Have you noticed any fever, fatigue, or muscle aches accompanying these skin and mouth lesions?

Have you recently been exposed to anyone with a similar rash, or do you recall a recent illness?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Captopril-induced Stomatitis/Mucositis with Bullous Skin Lesions (Drug-induced Mucocutaneous reaction).

I am ready to conclude the evaluation based on the clear link between your recent initiation of captopril and the development of painful oral and genital ulcers alongside forearm blisters.
